bills.summary: Extends free school meal support to cover school holidays for eligible children, so help isn't limited to term time.
benefits: Supporters say it tackles 'holiday hunger' and eases pressure on low-income families.
negatives: Critics question the ongoing cost and whether the money could be targeted more precisely.

bills.summary: Updates Northern Ireland's pension regulation, largely to keep it in step with changes already made in the rest of the UK.
benefits: Supporters say it better protects pension savers and keeps rules aligned with Great Britain.
negatives: Critics say any divergence or added complexity could burden schemes operating across the UK.

bills.summary: Sets out rules around the display of flags and emblems on public property and shared spaces.
benefits: Supporters say clear rules reduce tension and confusion about what can be displayed where.
negatives: Critics argue it is difficult to enforce neutrally and risks inflaming divisions.

bills.summary: Removes the legal basis for onshore oil and gas exploration and fracking in Northern Ireland.
benefits: Supporters say it protects the environment and rules out fracking.
negatives: Critics argue it closes off a possible domestic energy and economic option.

bills.summary: Concerns school uniform rules and affordability, including requirements around items such as trousers.
benefits: Supporters say it can lower the cost of school uniforms for families.
negatives: Critics question whether legislation is needed beyond what schools already decide locally.

bills.summary: Aims to grow the number of teachers qualified to teach through Irish, to meet demand for Irish-medium education.
benefits: Supporters say it secures the future of Irish-medium schooling.
negatives: Critics question the cost and prioritisation of one education sector over others.

bills.summary: Updates the rules governing credit unions in Northern Ireland.
benefits: Supporters say it lets credit unions offer more services and grow.
negatives: Critics say any widening of financial services needs strong member protections.

bills.summary: Extends age-discrimination protections to goods, facilities and services, beyond the workplace.
benefits: Supporters say it ends unfair treatment of people purely because of their age.
negatives: Critics worry about the compliance burden on businesses and unclear exemptions.

bills.summary: Strengthens protection for trees, including rules against unjustified felling.
benefits: Supporters say it protects green spaces and helps tackle pollution.
negatives: Critics worry about the impact on development and on landowner rights.

bills.summary: Updates rules on water management, sustainable drainage and flood management in Northern Ireland.
benefits: Supporters say it improves flood resilience as the climate changes.
negatives: Critics question implementation cost and whether drainage rules could delay building.

bills.summary: Concerns the temporary withdrawal of maternity services at Daisy Hill Hospital and the future of maternity care in the Southern Trust.
benefits: Supporters of the motion want services restored so families aren't forced to travel further.
negatives: Opponents point to staffing shortages that can make safe, immediate restoration difficult.

bills.summary: Calls for coordinated action to unlock the potential of tourism across the island of Ireland.
benefits: Supporters say it grows the visitor economy and supports jobs.
negatives: Critics question the focus on cross-border coordination over other priorities.

bills.summary: Concerns proposed cuts to BBC Northern Ireland services and their impact on local news and programming.
benefits: Supporters say local programming is vital to Northern Ireland's media and identity.
negatives: Opponents argue the BBC must live within its budget like any other service.

bills.summary: Concerns the early removal scheme for foreign national offenders and a proposed expansion of it.
benefits: Supporters say early removal reduces prison costs and population.
negatives: Critics raise concerns about fairness and whether public safety is fully protected.
